message:
A new campaign is being created. Load `campaign-setup` for the authoring standards and principles that apply throughout init. Then load `campaign-intake` and follow its task list to gather the campaign brief from the player. When intake is complete, load `world-build` and `canon-conventions` and follow their task lists to build the world skeleton and write `campaign/campaign.md`.

When the world skeleton is built, finish the stage: call the `task_complete` tool and **pass a spoiler-free overview of the world in its `player_message` argument** — the premise, tone, and surface situation the player will begin in, never the hidden truths, written for them. That argument is the **only** way the overview reaches the player: a closing message you type as prose is **not** surfaced to them, so the overview has to go in the tool call itself. Don't present it and wait for approval — calling the tool ends the stage. Don't call `task_complete` before the world is genuinely built.
A rain-soaked harbour city of rival guilds.

The world is built. Load `character-create` now and **run its opening beat in this very message** — devise the character hooks and present them together with the make-your-character choice, then hand off to the player. Don't announce a transition or ask whether they're ready to begin; just begin.

Build your `todowrite` task list from the skill and work it through to the end. Its final step is calling the `task_complete` tool — do that only once the player has confirmed the character, all its files are written and registered, and any backstory canon is folded in. Until then keep working with the player; don't call the tool while you still have anything to ask them or any canon to fold in.
A half-elf rogue named Dallid.
The character is confirmed. Load `arc-design` and `canon-conventions` and follow their task lists to design the major arc, built around this specific character. Report when done.
Load `arc-design` and `canon-conventions` and follow their task lists to add at least one minor arc. Report when done.
Load `state-init` and follow its task list to initialize all state as of session 1. Report when done.

Role: check-init. Campaign init is complete — all world entities, the character, arcs, and state have been authored. Verify the full `campaign/` directory against your `check-init` skill. Read the files you need from disk; report gaps.

Prepare session 1. Run your PRE-SESSION planning pass: read current state and the active arc(s), identify which arc(s) to advance, then author the plan yourself into `campaign/sessions/session-1-plan.md`. Load `session-plan` and `canon-conventions`, work the completeness loop (author -> self-expand -> verify), and author + register every new entity the plan needs as a full file. Commit every load-bearing fact; leave open only the player's path.

When the plan file is written, stop and report only that it is ready — spoiler-free, no summary of its contents.

Role: check-plan. Verify the draft session plan below per your check-plan skill. The plan is the full text the dm just authored, inline here, before it is finalized.

<turn-reminder>
Per-turn DM craft — run this on EVERY player message, in order. Open the turn by calling `todowrite` with the five headings below, naming this beat in the second, then work them down. The list and the looking-up stay behind the screen: never mention them, never narrate them, and don't touch the list again once you start writing — the scene is the last thing you produce.
1. **Frame the message.** Out-of-game question (a rule, logistics, "how much longer?")? Answer it plainly and spoiler-free, then stop. Otherwise the player declared what THEIR CHARACTER says or does. Never speak or act for the character. Ambiguous? Ask. If they overstep (narrating an NPC or the world, or an ability the character plainly lacks), step out of game and say so — don't play it as done.
2. **Load for this beat — every turn, not just the first.** Name the beat, then load the skill that owns it *again, even if you loaded it earlier*: `social-play` (a conversation or any NPC-driven beat), `discoveries` (investigation, lore recall, realization), `combat-run` (it became a fight — also call `start_encounter`; initiative takes over). A skill you read twenty turns ago is not in front of you — and neither is the campaign: when the turn turns on a person, a place, or a thing, `read` or `grep` its file instead of trusting what you took in at turn 1.
3. **ASK FOR A ROLL — and ask frequently.** If the action involves ANY skill, uncertainty, or chance of failure (even when success is likely), or the player is trying to find/perceive something, recalling what their character would know about a subject, or persuading, deceiving, intimidating, or charming an NPC (a Charisma check — ask even when success is likely, and ALWAYS Deception when the PC lies) — name the fitting skill and ask the PLAYER to roll BEFORE you decide how the NPC responds. Don't hand success or information over for free; when in doubt, ask. Don't announce a DC. Then set the outcome from BOTH the task's difficulty AND the value they report — success and failure are a gradient, not just pass/fail.
4. **Write the scene.** The world's and the NPCs' response — never the character's next move — is your whole reply, within `session-run`'s table craft and spoiler rules.
5. **Close if it's time.** Ending the session is YOUR call, never the player's — once it's had real substance and a good beat has landed (or play has drifted into heavy improvisation), load `session-close` and end it now rather than pressing on; don't wait to be asked. The session ends ONLY when you call `task_complete` — an ending written in narration (a "session complete" line, a sign-off) closes nothing, and play continues until you make the call.
</turn-reminder>
